coverage.note: The four placements are every search term this product’s campaigns served, redistributed — so they cover the whole product rather than a segment of it. They will not match the tile to the decimal: this split is attributed by CAMPAIGN and the tile by ASIN, which on product 59 is $27,484.86 of term spend against a $25,719.98 tile. The gap is the attribution, not a missing placement.

effBid.note: Lines are the SPEND-WEIGHTED mean effective bid — the bid set on each target that served this row, times its campaign's modifier for the slot. Off Amazon has a bar and no line: Sponsored Products carries no modifier for it, so there is no lever to draw. Read a line against the bar under it — that is the bid, and that is the share it bought.

conversion.note: Bars are each day's own estimated CLICKS at that placement. Lines are the conversion rate over the 7 days ENDING on that day — a deliberately different grain, because a placement conversion rate needs a campaign with at least 10 orders behind it and a single day almost never has one: measured on this segment, a day-grain line draws 7 of 30 days at Top of Search and 4 of 30 at Rest of Search. Off Amazon has bars and no line — its sales are too sparse to rate, the same ruling that keeps it off CTR and ACOS.

estimate: Amazon reports placement per CAMPAIGN and performance per KEYWORD, never together. Every placement figure here distributes this row’s own traffic across its parent campaigns’ placement shares — the same estimator the table below uses, run one day at a time.
notes: Sales, orders and every rate built on them carry 7-day attribution: the trailing seven days are still filling in and read LOW. The newest day is also a partial day. Compare settled windows with settled windows.

Read coverage first: a syntax group's split resolves to the terms the group OWNS, so it covers only part of the group row and says how much. A campaign's CVR per placement is drawn only where it has 10+ orders in the period.
